title: Register the SDK in the uv workspace and regenerate the lock
summary: The root pyproject.toml depends on assayer-plugin-sdk==0.1.2, a workspace package under packages/assayer-plugin-sdk that was neither a uv workspace member nor a declared source and is not published to a registry. As a result uv lock could not resolve the project and uv.lock could not be regenerated; the lock was missing the SDK dependency and earlier changes had to hand-edit it. This change registers the packages/ distributions as uv workspace members, declares assayer-plugin-sdk as a workspace source, and regenerates uv.lock with uv lock. The regenerated lock adds only the workspace packages; there are no unrelated version changes. The change is uv-only: the added [tool.uv.*] configuration affects local workspace resolution and lock generation, not the pip distribution split, the published dependency metadata, or any runtime contract, so the release surface is unchanged despite the release-engineering change type.

platform: Release engineering owns the distribution split and its lockfile
plugin: No plugin change; ordinary plugins remain data-only

forbiddenResponsibilities: The lock regeneration must not introduce unrelated dependency upgrades
The workspace registration must not publish or bundle an ordinary plugin as a Python distribution
The change must not alter the root package's public dependencies or extras
acceptance: uv lock --check succeeds at the repository root
uv.lock records assayer-plugin-sdk against the workspace package
the uv.lock diff adds only the workspace packages, with no unrelated version changes
scripts/run_tests.py fast and full stay green

humanApproval.decision: Internal-only packaging reproducibility fix carried out under the mandate in #assayer-group:4c84ee19; the unresolvable lock was confirmed and scoped with @assayer_rev on 2026-09-17.
